$comment: Committed so every clone inherits it.
These two hooks are what make Obsidian OPTIONAL. With Obsidian open, its Git
plugin handles syncing continuously. Without it, these hooks give you the
same guarantee at the two moments that matter: you start with everyone's
latest, and your work is never left sitting only on your laptop.
SessionStart: pull before you read anything. --autostash protects any
Stop: fires when Claude finishes responding. Commits and pushes only if
something actually changed, and only tracked/shared paths. The pre-commit
guard still runs, so an unsafe change is blocked here exactly as it would be
anywhere else. Quiet on success; speaks up only on failure or a block.
Deliberately NOT --no-verify. If the guard blocks, the work stays local and
the message explains why. That is the control working, not a fault.
Stop guards its own existence before running: a vault mid-scaffold (new-kb
still copying, or this file present before SETUP/hooks/ is) must not surface
a scary 'No such file or directory' for something that isn't a fault.

hooks.command: git pull --rebase --autostash --quiet 2>&1 || echo 'Vault sync: could not pull. Your work is safe — post a screenshot in the project Slack channel if this repeats.'
